meta.purpose: Machine-readable traceability backbone for the v2 implementation. Story numbers are the contract; ticket text is the summary.
meta.pathRationale: v1 exists as working code (~5100 lines of dependency-free vanilla ES modules in src/js/ plus a buildable Swift WKWebView shell in shell-macos/). The plan's Path A therefore holds: LZP-402 and LZP-403 stay in scope, E4 is 29 pts, total ~239 pts.
meta.storyToTicketRule: stories[].tickets is the union of the plan's §9 traceability table and every ticket whose acceptance criteria cite that story in §4. Empty array means the plan is silent.

stories.text: By default I'm in solo mode and nothing has changed from v1 — no account, no network activity, no prompts; the family features exist only behind an explicit "Familienkreis erstellen / beitreten" entry point in settings.
I create a Familienkreis with a name ("Familie Weber"), automatically become its admin, and receive a shareable invite code/link, so setup is one screen.

Mom joins by pasting the invite code into her app and choosing a display name and a personal color — no email, no password, no registration form — so a non-technical family member gets in within a minute.
All members see the member list (name, color, initial), so everyone knows who's in the circle.
Invite codes are single-use, expire after 7 days, and are revocable by the admin, so a leaked link can't haunt the family.
I can change my display name and color anytime and it propagates to everyone's boards, so identity stays current without admin involvement.
Everything I create is private by default — joining a family changes nothing about existing or new entries until I explicitly share them — so oversharing is structurally impossible.

Every note and bar has one of three visibility levels: Privat (only me), Belegt (others see that the day/range is taken, and by whom, but no text), Geteilt (others see everything) — so I can coordinate without disclosing.
I change an entry's visibility with a three-state control in its selected state and popover, two clicks maximum, so privacy management never feels like administration.
A personal category can set a default visibility for new entries in it (e.g., category "Familie" ⇒ Geteilt), so routine sharing costs zero extra clicks while the global default stays private.
I can change visibility at any time; a downgrade removes the entry (or its details) from other members' boards at the next sync, so nothing shared is shared forever.
My shared and busy entries carry a small badge on my own board, so I always see my exposure at a glance and never have to wonder what Mom can see.

A Belegt entry appears on others' boards as a neutral block with my color/initial and the word "Belegt" — duration and owner are deliberately visible, the content deliberately not — so "I'm away, don't plan with me" works without explanation.
stories.note: Scope-lever #3 (addendum §10) and Decision D5. LZP-701 publishes the client-side-redacted op; full content never leaves the device.

stories.text: Shared and Belegt entries from other members appear on my board automatically in their date rows, so family plans live exactly where my plans live.

Color logic: my entries always render in my category colors (my board stays mine); others' entries render in the member's personal color with an initial chip ("M") — so "whose is this?" is answered before "what is it?".
stories.note: Decision D4 confirms the person-color rule before LZP-801 design.

stories.text: The legend gains a member section: each member with color and a visibility toggle, so I can hide Papa's entries the same way I hide a category (4.3).
Family entries obey all v1 density rules — lanes cap (3.8), "+n" overflow (2.4), truncation (2.5) — so a busy family can never break the board's legibility.

Entries added or changed by others since my last session carry a quiet "neu" dot that fades once I've seen them — no popups, no counters, no push — so I notice change the way I'd notice new ink on a wall calendar.
Hover/popover shows attribution: "von Mama · geteilt · geändert So.", so provenance is one glance away but never printed on the board.
A per-device density setting (Kompakt / Komfort) slightly increases row height and font size on that machine only — Mom's display and eyes are not mine — accepting horizontal scroll as the trade.
stories.note: The only [Could] in v2 and scope-lever #1 (addendum §10). LZP-808 is S10 stretch only.

stories.text: By default only the owner can edit or delete an entry; other members view — so nobody's plans can be rewritten behind their back.
An entry-level flag "Familie darf bearbeiten" opts one entry into co-editing (the family vacation bar both of us drag around), so collaboration exists exactly where invited and nowhere else.
stories.note: Scope-lever #2 (addendum §10): owner-only editing is livable if v2 must shrink.

stories.text: As admin I can unshare any entry from the family space — it reverts to owner-private, it is never deleted — so moderation is possible but non-destructive, and I still can't read what was never shared.
My ⌘Z undoes only my own actions; other members' changes never appear in my undo stack, so undo stays predictable in a shared world.

If two people edit the same co-editable entry near-simultaneously, the later change wins per field, attribution updates (17.6), and only the person whose in-flight edit lost sees a quiet inline notice — conflicts at family scale are rare and must be treated as boring.
Deletions propagate to all boards; my undo of my own deletion restores the entry as a new shared operation, so even destructive acts stay reversible for their author.
The app is fully functional offline — create, edit, move, everything — and queues changes locally; sync happens when connectivity returns, so a train ride never interrupts planning.

(amended v2.1) My changes upload within seconds of saving; others' changes arrive automatically — on app focus and every ~30–60 s while the app is open (serverless pull, Section 3). There is no sync button and no manual refresh anywhere.
stories.note: Amended in place by v2.1 (serverless pull cadence); no UX copy may promise "live".

stories.text: Sync status is silent when healthy; only pending-offline or a real error produces a small, unobtrusive indicator — v1's "silence is the design" (F11) extends to the network.
I can pair my own second Mac (desktop + laptop): my entire board — including private entries — syncs end-to-end encrypted between my devices only, so "multi-desktop" works for one person too.
stories.note: Scope-lever #4 (addendum §10).

stories.text: Adding a device means entering a short pairing code shown on an existing device (key transfer), not a password-reset flow — there are no passwords in this product.
After long offline periods everything merges cleanly on return — including month rolls and yearly repeats that occurred meanwhile — so a laptop opened after three weeks just catches up.
As admin I can invite, revoke invites, remove members, rename the space, and transfer the admin role to another member, so the circle stays maintainable without support tickets.
Removing a member deletes their shared/Belegt entries from all family boards and their access — their private data on their own machine is untouched, because it was never ours.

Leaving voluntarily has the same effect, self-initiated; other members' shared entries disappear from my board, my own entries all revert to private and stay with me — nobody ever loses their own data by leaving.
As admin I can delete the entire Familienkreis: server data is purged, every member reverts to a fully intact solo board.

Even as admin, I structurally cannot see other members' private entries or the contents of their Belegt entries — the admin role grants space management, not surveillance; this is enforced by encryption, not by policy.
In v2, each user belongs to at most one Familienkreis, so the mental model stays as simple as the family it serves.
Shared and Belegt entries are end-to-end encrypted; only member devices hold keys — the server stores and relays ciphertext it cannot read.
Private entries never leave my machines except end-to-end encrypted to my own paired devices (19.4) — no family key can ever decrypt them.

(amended v2.1) The app documents plainly what the server side can see — pseudonymous IDs, timestamps, IP addresses in transit, encrypted blob sizes — and names the processors (Vercel, Prisma Postgres; EU/Frankfurt region), so trust is informed, not marketed.
Still no analytics, no tracking, no third-party services beyond the sync endpoint.

Network scope, replacing 13.4: in solo mode the app makes zero network requests; with a Familienkreis it talks to exactly one sync endpoint and nothing else. The v1 property survives as a scoped guarantee.
stories.note: Successor property to v1's 13.4 (A1).

stories.text: The app ships as a single DMG (≈15 MB, comfortably under mail attachment limits); installing is open → drag to Programme → launch, so Mom's entire setup is one email attachment and one drag. The same email carries the GitHub-Releases download link as fallback for providers that block DMG attachments.

First launch handles macOS quarantine gracefully: a signed and notarized build simply opens; in the unsigned fallback, a first-run screen walks through the Systemeinstellungen unlock in two illustrated steps — mandatory if unsigned, because macOS 15+ removed the right-click-open bypass.
stories.note: Supersedes the v1 §4 Gatekeeper note (A12). Which branch ships depends on Decision D1.

stories.text: The app checks for updates on launch and roughly daily, downloads quietly in the background, and applies on the next start — after the first email, nobody ever downloads anything manually again.

An available update announces itself only as a quiet "Update verfügbar" hint (app menu and settings), never a modal; one click restarts into the new version, and simply quitting applies it on next launch.
Every device — my two Macs and Mom's — follows the same single release channel: when I publish a version, the whole family converges on it automatically, with no per-person support rounds.

Updates are cryptographically signed with the app's updater key and verified before installing, so an email-distributed app cannot grow a hijackable update path — a device installs authentic builds or nothing.
stories.note: LZP-304 (op envelopes) is listed in the plan as "22.6-adjacent" — related versioned-ciphertext work, not a mapped AC.

stories.text: Updates never touch user data; schema migrations (11.6) run after the swap. If a server protocol change ever requires a minimum client version, the update manifest enforces it and outdated clients say so in one plain sentence instead of failing quietly.

Releases flow from GitHub: tagging a version triggers the build (GitHub Actions) and publishes DMG + update manifest to GitHub Releases, while the sync server deploys from the same repository to Vercel — one git tag, and the entire product, server and every desktop, moves forward together.
A crowded day shows the first two notes plus "+n"; clicking expands a popover with the full stack, so narrow columns never silently hide entries.
stories.note: Carried into v2: the popover gains the sharing cluster (A7) and family entries must obey the "+n" overflow rule (17.4).

stories.text: Notes cap at ~80 characters, truncate with ellipsis, and show full text on hover — keeping rows thin is what keeps 12 months on one screen.
stories.note: Must not regress: 17.4 requires family entries to obey v1 truncation.

stories.text: Parallel lanes cap at 3 per day; further overlaps compress into a "+n" marker with tooltip, so extreme weeks stay legible.
stories.note: Must not regress: 17.4 requires family entries to obey the v1 lanes cap.

stories.text: I toggle a category's visibility in the legend, so I can isolate e.g. Work when planning around deadlines.
stories.note: The legend becomes two sections (A3); per-member toggles mirror this control (17.3). Categories are never synced.

stories.text: Colors come from a fixed palette of ~10 distinguishable, print-safe tones instead of a free picker, so the legend stays readable on screen and paper.
stories.note: Member colors draw from the same ~10-tone palette but are a separate namespace; the join flow prevents collisions (addendum §9).

stories.text: ⌘Z undoes / ⇧⌘Z redoes my recent changes (~50 steps), covering create, edit, move, resize, and delete — so no drag or delete is ever scary. Import is excluded; it has its own confirmation instead.
stories.note: LZP-405 reworks undo as inverse ops scoped to own actions (18.4); v1 ⌘Z semantics must be preserved solo.

stories.text: Unlike public holidays, Ferien are negotiated per state and published only ~2–3 years ahead — so the bundled dataset has a visible horizon ("Ferien-Daten bis Sommer 2028" in settings), beyond which shading is simply absent; app updates refresh the data.
stories.note: A11 gives 7.4 its delivery vehicle: bundled Ferien datasets ride the normal update channel. No separate data download may exist (21.5).

stories.text: Entries that roll out of view are kept in storage, not deleted, so history survives and reappears if I pin an earlier start month.
stories.note: A9: history retention covers family entries while I am a member; leaving removes others' entries from my history too (20.3). My own entries' history is always fully mine.

stories.text: Date changes while the app is running — midnight passes, or the Mac wakes from sleep days later — update the today marker and trigger the month-roll live, no restart needed.
stories.note: Long-offline convergence (19.6) must survive month rolls that happened meanwhile.

stories.text: A "repeats yearly" checkbox on a note makes it reappear on the same date every year, so birthdays survive the roll into the next year.
stories.note: A4: yearly repeats can be shared — Oma's birthday entered once, visible to everyone, forever. seriesId lands in LZP-404.

stories.text: Editing or deleting a repeating note applies to the whole series, so there's exactly one object to maintain — no exception logic.
stories.note: A4: visibility is series-level (no per-year exceptions), which is what keeps 9.3's one-object rule intact.

stories.text: Each month column has a small free-text area beneath it, so undated thoughts ("book cabin?") live next to the month they belong to.
stories.note: A5: month scratchpads stay private in v2; a shared family scratchpad is explicitly deferred. No ticket by design — the guard is that scratchpad content must never enter the family op stream.

stories.text: One click exports the entire state (entries, categories, settings) as a single JSON file, so backups and machine moves are trivial.
stories.note: A2: export additionally contains my identity keys and my shared/Belegt entries with flags; other members' entries are never exported.

stories.text: Importing a JSON restores that state after an explicit "replace current board?" confirmation, so recovery is one action and never an accident.
stories.note: A2: import restores my data and re-joins my Familienkreis if the keys are present.

stories.text: The app keeps the last 7 daily snapshots with one-click restore, so yesterday's bad idea is recoverable even after undo history is gone.
stories.note: LZP-403 text requires existing board.json plus snapshots to migrate losslessly on first v2 launch.

stories.text: The file carries a schema version, and newer app versions migrate it automatically, so updating the app never strands your data.
stories.note: Also referenced by 22.7: updates never touch user data; migrations run after the swap.

stories.text: Printing respects the current layer and category toggles — what I see is what prints — so I control the output with the tools I already have.
stories.note: A8 confirms 12.3 unchanged and extends it: print includes family entries and honors member toggles.

stories.text: The app makes zero network requests — not "we don't collect data" but architecturally can't — privacy as a property, not a promise.
stories.note: Superseded by 21.5 (A1). The v1 wording stays true for solo mode and should be quoted that way in about/marketing copy. LZP-1002 asserts it as an automated test.

stories.text: UI language is German by default (the content world is German — Feiertage, Ferien), with an English toggle in settings.
stories.note: Must not regress and is a Definition-of-Done gate for every ticket: strings in DE and EN. The plan maps no ticket to it because it is a cross-cutting DoD item.

stories.text: ⌘F opens a slim search field; matching notes and bars light up, everything else dims; Enter steps through hits (⇧Enter backwards); Esc restores the board.
stories.note: A6: find searches family entries too (shared text, Belegt matches on owner name); dimming logic unchanged.

amendments.text: 13.4 (superseded). "Zero network by architecture" becomes the scoped guarantee of 21.5. v1's wording may remain true for solo mode and should be quoted that way in about/marketing copy.

11.2 / 11.3 (export & import). Export contains my data: private entries, my shared/Belegt entries (with flags), categories, settings, and my identity keys (this is the recovery artifact — say so in the file's header comment). Other members' entries are not exported; they re-arrive via sync. Import restores my data and re-joins my Familienkreis if the keys are present.

F4 (legend). The legend becomes two sections: Meine Kategorien (unchanged, personal, local) and Familie (members with color + visibility toggle, 17.3). Categories are never synced; they remain a private organizational system.

F9 (repeats). Yearly repeats can be shared — this is the killer family feature: Oma's birthday entered once, visible to everyone, forever. Series-level visibility (the whole series is Privat/Belegt/Geteilt, no per-year exceptions) keeps 9.3's one-object rule.
F10 (scratchpads). Month scratchpads stay private in v2. A shared family scratchpad per month is explicitly deferred (Section 11) — free-text merging is a conflict swamp with little payoff.
amendments.note: The only unticketed amendment; it defers a feature by design. The implementation guard is negative: scratchpad content must never enter the family op stream.

amendments.text: 14.1 (find). Find searches family entries too (shared text, Belegt matches on owner name); dimming logic unchanged.
2.4 / 3.x (popovers). Entry popovers gain the sharing cluster: three-state visibility control (16.3), co-edit flag (18.2), attribution line (17.6).
amendments.note: "3.x" is the plan's own wording — it means the bar popovers/selected states of F3 collectively; the addendum names no single F3 story.

amendments.text: 12.3 (print). Unchanged and confirmed: print renders what's visible — including family entries and honoring member toggles. A family wall poster is now a two-click product.
8.4 (history). History retention covers family entries while I'm a member; leaving removes others' entries from my history too (20.3). My own entries' history is always fully mine.

F13 (settings). Settings gains a Familie section: create/join, member list, admin panel (F20), sync status detail, Datenschutz text (21.3), device pairing (19.5). First-run flow remains untouched (Principle 7).

7.4 (Schulferien refresh mechanism). "App updates refresh the data" now has its vehicle: bundled Ferien datasets ride the normal update channel (F22). The settings horizon display simply reflects the shipped dataset; no separate data download exists.

v1 Section 4, distribution note (superseded). The v1 Gatekeeper note ("right-click → Open once") predates macOS 15's removal of that bypass and the email-distribution decision. Replaced by 22.2: preferred path signed + notarized (Developer ID), fallback path the guided Systemeinstellungen unlock screen.

tickets.title: Release workflow
tickets.text: GitHub Actions: tag → Tauri universal macOS build → DMG + update artifacts to GitHub Releases. Bundled Schulferien datasets ride along (A11).

tickets.title: Auto-updater
tickets.text: Tauri updater: signed manifest, check on launch + daily, background download, apply on relaunch; single stable channel for all devices.

tickets.title: Update UX
tickets.text: Quiet "Update verfügbar" hint (app menu + settings), restart-to-update, quit-applies. No modals.

tickets.title: Minimum-version enforcement
tickets.text: Manifest min-version gate + plain-language outdated screen.

tickets.title: Signing & notarization
tickets.text: Developer ID cert in CI, codesign + notarize + staple; quarantine-clean first launch.
tickets.note: Developer-ID procurement (D1) starts in S1 because of Apple's admin lead time, even though the ticket lands in S10 before the Mom test.

tickets.title: Unsigned fallback screen
tickets.text: First-run guided Systemeinstellungen unlock, two illustrated steps. Only if D1 = no.
tickets.conditional: Only exists if Decision D1 = no

tickets.text: Prisma models Space/Member/Invite/Op per §3 sketch; Frankfurt region; migrations in CI.
tickets.note: AC is addendum §3 (server schema sketch) plus addendum §9 constraints (EU/Frankfurt region), not a numbered story.

tickets.title: Op endpoints
tickets.text: Append (push) + fetch-since-seq (pull) with device-signature auth; idempotent, ordered per space.

tickets.title: Space & invite endpoints
tickets.text: Create space, invite create/redeem/revoke (single-use, 7-day expiry), member list/update.

tickets.title: Lifecycle endpoints
tickets.text: Member remove/leave, role transfer, space rename/delete with full cascade purge.

tickets.title: Abuse basics
tickets.text: Rate limits, payload caps, structured logs that never contain content.

tickets.title: Protocol versioning
tickets.text: Client version header; server supports current + previous protocol; compat test harness in CI.

tickets.title: Server metadata inventory
tickets.text: Written inventory of everything the server can observe → feeds Datenschutz copy.
tickets.note: Sprint conflict: LZP-1001 declares a dep on this ticket but is scheduled in S9, one sprint earlier.

tickets.title: Crypto spike & ADR
tickets.text: libsodium-based design: device keypairs, per-space symmetric key, per-op envelope; written threat notes. Timeboxed.
tickets.note: Risk R1's mitigation: timeboxed; overrun in S2 is the early warning.

tickets.title: Device identity
tickets.text: Keygen on first run, storage in macOS Keychain via Tauri, stable device ID.

tickets.title: Space keys & rotation
tickets.text: Create/wrap/unwrap space key per member device; rotate on every membership change so removed members cannot decrypt future ops.

tickets.title: Op envelopes
tickets.text: Encrypt/sign/decrypt/verify pipeline; versioned ciphertext format.
tickets.note: Plan lists this as "22.6-adjacent" — related to the signed-update trust model without being one of its ACs.

tickets.title: Backup v2
tickets.text: Export includes identity keys + own entries (private + shared-by-me), never others'; import restores identity and re-joins the Kreis.

tickets.title: Device pairing protocol
tickets.text: Short pairing code shown on existing device; key transfer via relay; both-ends confirmation.

tickets.title: Local op-log ADR
tickets.text: Op shapes, ULIDs, tombstones, per-field LWW timestamps, materialization strategy.
tickets.note: AC is addendum §3 plus "18.5-ready" — the ADR must make per-field LWW possible, not implement it.

tickets.title: Storage retrofit
tickets.text: Convert the v1 store to op-log + materialized state; the entire v1 feature set stays green (regression suite).
tickets.note: AC is "all v1 behavior unchanged" — the regression gate is the complete v1 story set (F1-F14, 79 stories), not a subset. Risk R5; on this machine the target is src/js/store.js.

tickets.title: v1→v2 migration
tickets.text: Existing board.json + snapshots migrate losslessly on first v2 launch.

tickets.title: Entry metadata
tickets.text: ownerId, visibility, coEdit, seriesId on notes/bars; series-level visibility for repeats.

tickets.title: Undo rework
tickets.text: Undo/redo as inverse ops, strictly scoped to own actions; v1 ⌘Z semantics preserved solo.

tickets.title: Merge property tests
tickets.text: Property-based harness: op reorder/duplicate/interleave ⇒ convergent state.
tickets.note: Plan says "18.5 groundwork" — convergence must be provable before LZP-904 implements the conflict UI. Risk R2.

tickets.title: Sync engine client
tickets.text: Outbox queue, push-on-save, pull on focus + 30–60 s poll, offline queueing, backoff.
tickets.depsNote: Plan writes the third dep as "40x" — the E4 op-log core collectively (LZP-401/402/403/404), not one named ticket.

tickets.text: Private entries sync E2E between own devices only; no family key can ever apply.

tickets.text: Clean Mac, real email with DMG + code, unassisted install & join; fix what stumbles.
tickets.note: Decision D1 does not gate this ticket but determines its quality (signed build vs. guided unlock screen).

tickets.title: Perf pass
tickets.text: 60 fps drag with 8-member × 2-year fixture; sync CPU/battery sanity.

tickets.title: Ops runbook
tickets.text: Vercel/Prisma runbook, key-loss support script, release checklist.
tickets.note: AC is addendum §3 (infrastructure decision record), not a numbered story.

decisions.question: Apple Developer ID (99 €/yr) — sign & notarize?
decisions.recommendation: Yes (addendum open question 8). Signing + notarization deletes the scariest screen a non-technical family member would otherwise meet (22.2) and makes background updates trustworthy on modern macOS. Procurement starts in S1 because of Apple's admin lead time, even though LZP-105 lands in S10.
decisions.note: LZP-106 exists only if the answer is no. LZP-1006 is not gated but its quality depends on the answer. Risk R4.

decisions.question: Confirm EU/Frankfurt region for Vercel functions and Prisma Postgres.
decisions.recommendation: Yes (addendum open question 9). Frankfurt is already a fixed constraint in addendum §9 and is named in the Datenschutz copy (21.3).

decisions.question: Confirm "GitHub sync" = deploy-on-push reading.
decisions.recommendation: Confirm §3 as written: Vercel's GitHub integration deploys the server on push to main. The alternative reading (syncing data through GitHub) would veto §3 entirely.

decisions.question: Person-color rule for foreign entries (17.2) — accept, or argue for shared categories instead?
decisions.recommendation: Accept 17.2 as specced (addendum open question 2): my entries in my category colors, others' entries in the member's personal color with an initial chip.

decisions.question: Belegt confirmed in v2.0, or deferred per addendum §10?
decisions.recommendation: Keep (addendum open question 3). Cutting Belegt is scope-lever #3 and weakens the product's core answer to "Mom doesn't need everything".
decisions.note: Also determines whether LZP-706 has any content.

decisions.question: Path A (retrofit an existing v1) or Path B (greenfield on the op-log from day one)?
decisions.recommendation: B if greenfield — build v1 on the op-log from day one, LZP-402/403 disappear, E4 shrinks to 16 pts, v2 lands in ~226 pts ≈ 9 sprints.
decisions.resolved: Path A. v1 exists as working code in this repository (~5100 lines of dependency-free vanilla ES modules in src/js/, plus a buildable Swift WKWebView shell in shell-macos/), so LZP-402 and LZP-403 stay in scope and the plan runs at ~239 pts ≈ 10 sprints.

constraints: Family scale target: 2–8 members — the design must be excellent at 2 and acceptable at 8, not the reverse. (addendum §9)
One Familienkreis per user (20.6). Exactly one admin at a time; the role is transferable (20.1). (addendum §9)
Member colors and category colors draw from the same ~10-tone palette but are separate namespaces; no two members share a color. (addendum §9)
Visibility is per entry, series-level for repeats (A4). No per-member visibility ("share with Mom but not Papa") in v2 — the circle is the unit of trust. (addendum §9)
Still no times of day: shared entries are all-day/multi-day, like everything else. YYYY-MM-DD survives the network intact. (addendum §9)
Server region: EU (Frankfurt) for both Vercel functions and Prisma Postgres; the sync endpoint remains the only remote the app ever contacts (21.5). (addendum §9)
One release channel ("stable") for all users and devices — no betas for family members. (addendum §9)
The server always supports the current and the previous client protocol version (addendum §3, 22.7). (addendum §9)
Vercel Hobby / Prisma free tiers assumed: non-commercial family use only; commercialization triggers a paid plan. (addendum §9)
Dates are plain YYYY-MM-DD. No times ⇒ no timezone or DST bugs, ever. (v1 §13)
Holiday granularity is the Bundesland (16 states; the selector also offers "nur bundesweite Feiertage"). Municipal specials (e.g. Augsburger Friedensfest) are out of scope. (v1 §13)
Feiertage are computed (fixed dates + Easter arithmetic + Buß- und Bettag) ⇒ no data horizon. Schulferien are bundled data ⇒ visible horizon in settings (7.4). (v1 §13)
Limits chosen for legibility, not tech: ~80-char notes, 3 bar lanes, ~5-line scratchpads, ~50 undo steps, 7 snapshots. (v1 §13)
